motivation: User asks whether individual model blocks need different initialization scales. Examine the exact local effect of scaling a linear map immediately before the existing finite-epsilon RMS.
objective: Separate changes to normalized forward values, physical-parameter gradients and radial/tangent conditioning; no initialization candidate or learning claim.
proof_targets: Lift the existing finite-epsilon identity R_eps(s*z)=R_(eps/s^2)(z), s>0, to a fixed linear parameter-to-activation map A.
Given a derivative D of loss(R_(eps/s^2)(A(w))) at w, the physical-parameter derivative of loss(R_eps(A(w))) at s*w is (1/s)*D. Keep the derivative hypothesis explicit.
Prove the matching coordinate RMS VJP rescaling identity, with nonnegative mean-square energy, positive epsilon and positive scale.
Increasing scale s>=1 makes the radial/tangent coefficient ratio eps/(s^2*m+eps) no larger; this is not a full-network condition number or an optimizer guarantee.

numerical_grid.construction: v repeats [1,1,-1,-1], t repeats [1,-1,1,-1], so both have unit RMS and are exactly orthogonal. W has columns a*v/2 and -a*v/2. The fixed linear input gives z=a*v. Compare independent physical parameter leaves s*W at epsilon and W at epsilon/s^2.
numerical_grid.references: Independent binary64 closed forms for outputs and radial/tangent VJPs, evaluated at represented amplitudes. Compare all physical-matrix gradients and the inverse-scale identity. Exact-zero reference vectors require exact zeros.
numerical_grid.policy: Keep every case and all failures. Do not loosen the threshold. Source validation and mathematical proof precede the numerical check.

limits: Real-arithmetic proofs retain finite epsilon. Numerical checks concern only the declared moderate-scale CPU grid, not a floating-point proof.

The linear map, downstream scalar loss and cotangent are fixed for each local comparison. Internal SwiGLU scales, simultaneous model changes, tied embedding/readout paths and optimizer trajectories are outside the identity.
The counterpart uses epsilon/s^2. Fixed-epsilon RMS is not exactly scale invariant, and inverse gradient scaling is not an exact same-epsilon training statement.
No optimizer updates, new task data or held-out scores, best initializer selection, current capacity/gain alteration, or repair of the ten unresolved full-stack numerical failures.
